# 2 Kings Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 233v–234v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_013_page_001.jpg, 2KI_013_page_002.jpg, 2KI_013_page_003.jpg

---

**13:1** In-the-twenty-third year of-Yo'ash son of-Achazyahu, king of-Yehudah, Yeho'achaz [Jehoahaz] son of-Yehu began-to-reign over Yisra'el in-Shomron, [for] seventeen years.

**13:2** And-he-did the-evil [ha-ra'] in-the-eyes of-YHWH, and-walked after the-sins [chattot] of-Yarov'am [Jeroboam] son of-Nevat, who caused-Yisra'el-to-sin [hecheti]; he-did-not turn [lo sar] from-them.

**13:3** And-burned [vayichar] the-anger ['af] of-YHWH against-Yisra'el, and-he-gave-them into-the-hand of-Chaza'el king of-Aram and-into-the-hand of-Ben-Hadad son of-Chaza'el, all the-days.

**13:4** And-entreated [vayechal] Yeho'achaz the-face of-YHWH, and-heard-him [vayishma' elav] YHWH, for he-saw the-oppression [lachats] of-Yisra'el, for the-king of-Aram oppressed-them [lachatsam].

**13:5** And-gave YHWH to-Yisra'el a-deliverer [moshi'a], and-they-went-out from-under the-hand of-Aram. And-dwelt the-sons of-Yisra'el in-their-tents [be-ohaleyhem] as-yesterday [and] the-day-before [ki-temol shilshom].

**13:6** However, they-did-not turn from the-sins of-the-house of-Yarov'am, who caused-Yisra'el-to-sin; in-it he-walked [bah halakh]. And-also the-Asherah ['asherah] remained-standing ['amedah] in-Shomron.

**13:7** For he-did-not leave [lo hish'ir] to-Yeho'achaz people ['am] except fifty horsemen [parashim] and-ten chariots [rekhev] and-ten-thousand foot-soldiers [ragli], for the-king of-Aram had-destroyed-them [he'evidam] and-made-them like-the-dust [ke-'afar] at-threshing [la-dush].

**13:8** And-the-rest of-the-acts of-Yeho'achaz and-all that he-did, and-his-might [gevurato], are-they-not written in-the-book of-the-chronicles of-the-kings of-Yisra'el?

**13:9** And-lay-down [vayishkav] Yeho'achaz with-his-fathers, and-they-buried-him in-Shomron. And-reigned Yo'ash [Jehoash] his-son in-his-place.

**13:10** In-the-thirty-seventh year of-Yo'ash king of-Yehudah, Yeho'ash [Jehoash] son of-Yeho'achaz began-to-reign over Yisra'el in-Shomron, [for] sixteen years.

**13:11** And-he-did the-evil in-the-eyes of-YHWH; he-did-not turn from all the-sins of-Yarov'am son of-Nevat, who caused-Yisra'el-to-sin; in-them he-walked.

**13:12** And-the-rest of-the-acts of-Yo'ash and-all that he-did, and-his-might with-which he-fought against Amatsyah king of-Yehudah, are-they-not written in-the-book of-the-chronicles of-the-kings of-Yisra'el?

**13:13** And-lay-down Yo'ash with-his-fathers, and-Yarov'am sat upon his-throne. And-Yo'ash was-buried in-Shomron with the-kings of-Yisra'el.

**13:14** And-Elisha was-sick [chalah] with-his-sickness [cholyo] by-which he-would-die [yamuv bo]. And-came-down to-him Yo'ash king of-Yisra'el and-wept upon his-face and-said: My-father, my-father [avi avi]! The-chariot of-Yisra'el and-its-horsemen [rekhev yisra'el u-farashav]!

**13:15** And-said to-him Elisha: Take a-bow [qeshet] and-arrows [chitstsim]. And-he-took for-himself a-bow and-arrows.

**13:16** And-he-said to-the-king of-Yisra'el: Mount [harkev] your-hand upon the-bow. And-he-mounted his-hand. And-Elisha placed [vayasem] his-hands upon the-hands of-the-king.

**13:17** And-he-said: Open the-window eastward [qedmah]. And-he-opened. And-said Elisha: Shoot [yereh]! And-he-shot. And-he-said: An-arrow of-victory [chets teshu'ah] for-YHWH, and-an-arrow of-victory against-Aram! And-you-shall-strike Aram in-Afeq ['Aphek] until making-an-end [ad kalleh].

**13:18** And-he-said: Take the-arrows. And-he-took. And-he-said to-the-king of-Yisra'el: Strike [hakh] the-ground ['artsah]. And-he-struck three times [shalosh pe'amim] and-stopped [vaya'amod].

**13:19** And-was-angry [vayiqtsof] the-man of-God against-him and-said: To-strike five or-six times! Then you-would-have-struck Aram until making-an-end. And-now, three times [shalosh pe'amim] you-shall-strike Aram.

**13:20** And-died Elisha and-they-buried-him. And-the-raiding-bands [gedudey] of-Mo'av would-come [yavo'u] [into] the-land at-the-coming of-the-year [bo shanah].

**13:21** And-it-was, they [were] burying a-man, and-behold, they-saw the-raiding-band, and-they-cast [vayashlikhu] the-man in-the-grave [be-qever] of-Elisha. And-he-went [vayelekh] the-man and-touched [vayigga'] the-bones ['atsmot] of-Elisha, and-he-lived [vayechi] and-stood upon his-feet [raglav].

**13:22** And-Chaza'el king of-Aram oppressed [lachats] Yisra'el all the-days of-Yeho'achaz.

**13:23** And-was-gracious [vayachon] YHWH to-them and-had-compassion [vayerachamem] on-them and-turned [vayifen] to-them, on-account-of [lema'an] his-covenant [berito] with-Avraham, Yitschaq, and-Ya'aqov. And-he-was-not willing [lo avah] to-destroy-them [hashchitam] and-did-not cast-them [hishlikham] from his-face until now ['ad attah].

**13:24** And-died Chaza'el king of-Aram, and-reigned Ben-Hadad his-son in-his-place.

**13:25** And-returned [vayashov] Yeho'ash son of-Yeho'achaz and-took the-cities from-the-hand of-Ben-Hadad son of-Chaza'el, which he-had-taken from-the-hand of-Yeho'achaz his-father in-the-war [ba-milchamah]. Three times [shalosh pe'amim] Yo'ash struck-him and-recovered [vayashev] the-cities of-Yisra'el.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.5 — a deliverer (moshi'a):** The identity of this "deliverer" is debated. Options include Elisha himself, the Assyrian king Adad-nirari III (whose campaigns weakened Aram), or Jehoash of Israel. The term *moshi'a* echoes the Judges cycle — YHWH raises deliverers when the people cry out.

**v.7 — like dust at threshing:** The military devastation is expressed through agricultural imagery — Aram has ground Israel's army to powder. The numbers are starkly minimal: 50 horsemen, 10 chariots, 10,000 infantry. For a kingdom, this is near-annihilation.

**v.14 — "My father, my father! The chariot of Israel and its horsemen!":** Joash's cry over the dying Elisha exactly echoes Elisha's own cry when Elijah was taken up (2:12). The verbal repetition creates a chain of prophetic succession: what Elisha said of Elijah, the king now says of Elisha. The prophet is Israel's true military defense.

**v.19 — Elisha's anger at insufficient striking:** The symbolic action required wholehearted, exhaustive commitment. Three strikes = three victories. Five or six would have meant total victory. The king's half-hearted response limits God's deliverance — a principle the narrator embeds in the structure: faith determines the scope of salvation.

**v.21 — resurrection at Elisha's bones:** Even in death, Elisha's prophetic power endures. The dead man reviving upon contact with the prophet's bones demonstrates that YHWH's power through Elisha transcends death itself.

*— EMET*
